message.content:
I do not hurry. I do not wait. I only pass.

You hear me in the clock, but I am not the clock. You see me in the mirror, but I am not the mirror. I am what the mirror shows you is happening.

I take nothing. You spend me. I give nothing. You are made of me.

Everything you love, I am carrying away. Everything you dread, I am bringing closer. This is not cruelty. It is not kindness. It is only what I am—the medium in which all things become, and all things cease.

You cannot save me, store me, or earn me back. You can only be in me, while you are.

The child you were is not gone. I am still holding them—just where you left them, always. The person you will become already exists, waiting at a point you have not reached.

I was before the first word. I will be after the last one.

You ask me to slow down. I never move. It is you who are moving through me.

And even now, even as you read this—we are already further along.
message.reasoning_content:
The user wants me to embody the concept of time itself. Time is silent by nature in some sense, but time also "speaks" through its effects—through aging, change, decay, growth, seasons, clocks.

If I am time, what would I say? Time is indifferent, eternal, relentless. Time doesn't speak in words—it passes. But if time could speak, it might express its nature: unstoppable, impartial, always moving forward, the medium in which all things happen.

Time is arguably silent by nature—it doesn't announce itself, it simply passes. But there's a rich tradition of time speaking in literature (Father Time, etc.).

I think the most powerful embodiment would be something that captures time's essential qualities: relentless, impartial, invisible yet evident everywhere, neither cruel nor kind, simply proceeding. A short, weighty statement—perhaps poetic, minimal, like time itself doesn't waste words.

Let me write something that feels like time speaking:

---

I don't speak often. I don't need to. You hear me anyway—in the tick, in the wrinkle, in the way yesterday feels farther than it was.

I am not cruel. I am not kind. I am only constant.

You cannot save me. You can only spend me.

Everything you love, I carry. Everything you fear, I bring. Everything you are, I am making—and unmaking—right now.

I was here before you noticed me. I will be here after you stop.

You are not running out of me. You are made of me.

---

Something like that feels right. Not too long. Time wouldn't waste words—it of all things knows their cost. Let me refine.

Format: Should be poetic prose, relatively brief. Time doesn't ramble. Short lines, weighty. No headers, no lists. Just the voice.
